cross_package_notes.note: Verified read-only downstream ingestion contract in applyFetchedItem / ingestItem: when len(item.Content) == 0 && item.URL != "", DataSourceService passes item.URL directly to CreateKnowledgeFromURL. Hardened IMA (fetchOneMedia for mediaTypeWeb) and RSS (resolveItem for item.Link) so non-http(s), userinfo-bearing, and SSRF-blocked URLs are rejected/stripped before FetchedItem emission.

Verified read-only caller compatibility via GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 1 ./internal/application/service/... ./internal/handler/... (exit 0): all exported symbols in internal/datasource and all 12 connector subpackages preserve exact signatures.

invariants_checked: ValidateConnectorBaseURL and NewConnectorHTTPClient enforce http/https schemes, non-empty hosts, SSRF safe-dialer validation blocking loopback/RFC1918/link-local/metadata IPs, cross-origin credential-stripping on redirects, and reject control characters, embedded userinfo, query strings, and URL fragments without echoing raw credential secrets in error messages.

ConnectorRegistry synchronizes concurrent Register, Get, and List calls under sync.RWMutex with deterministic sorted output, and ListAvailableConnectors returns deep-cloned ConnectorMetadata slices in deterministic order so caller mutations never corrupt global connector capabilities.

Scheduler guards nil/blank DataSource inputs in AddOrUpdate, fails closed without enqueuing duplicate sync tasks when HasRunningSync returns a repository error, and classifies wrapped asynq.ErrTaskIDConflict via errors.Is as SyncLogStatusCanceled rather than SyncLogStatusFailed.
SanitizeFileName strips path separators, dot-segments, and oversized UTF-8 titles safely on rune boundaries; zero legacy brand residues exist across all files.

findings.summary: ValidateConnectorBaseURL accepted embedded userinfo (https://user:pass@host), query strings (?override=1), URL fragments (#frag), and control characters, and echoed raw url.Parse errors containing embedded passwords when percent-encoding failed.

ConnectorRegistry accessed its internal connectors map without mutex synchronization (data race under concurrent Register/Get/List) and returned non-deterministic map iteration order; ListAvailableConnectors also aliased shared Capabilities backing slices and iterated an unsorted map.

Scheduler.AddOrUpdate dereferenced nil DataSource pointers and accepted blank IDs, triggerSync failed open to enqueue overlapping syncs when HasRunningSync returned a DB error, and wrapped asynq.ErrTaskIDConflict was checked with == instead of errors.Is (marking deduplicated tasks Failed instead of Canceled).

invariants_checked: Confluence Cloud and Server/DC BaseURL normalization enforces SSRF validation, preserves explicit ports on *.atlassian.net when auto-appending /wiki, rejects embedded userinfo/query/fragment/control characters, and rejects CRLF/control characters in PAT and Basic credentials without echoing secrets.
Resource IDs and upstream space/page/attachment IDs reject dot-segments ('.', '..'), slashes, backslashes, and control characters and apply url.PathEscape across all REST v1/v2 endpoints.

Authenticated REST API redirects are restricted to both same-origin and the configured BaseURL context path prefix (e.g. /wiki) so sibling reverse-proxied apps on the same host cannot receive PAT/Basic credentials, while attachment downloads strip auth headers on cross-origin redirects and bound reads with io.LimitReader.
CQL/v2 cursor pagination detects repeated cursors and caps page hops, and FetchAll/FetchIncremental fail closed on nil DataSourceConfig.

findings.summary: parseResourceID and Confluence REST v1/v2 path builders accepted dot-segment IDs ('.', '..') that traversed /rest/api/content/.. to /rest/api, normalizeBaseURL used parsed.Host instead of parsed.Hostname() (missing *.atlassian.net:443 Cloud suffix detection) and allowed embedded userinfo, and parseConfig accepted CRLF/control characters in credentials.

Authenticated Confluence API HTTP client allowed same-origin redirects escaping the configured BaseURL context path (e.g. /wiki -> /other-app) with PAT/Basic Authorization headers intact, and Connector.FetchAll panicked on nil DataSourceConfig before parseConfig ran.

invariants_checked: Access token caching, refresh, and 401/400 invalidation in client.go synchronize c.token and c.tokenExpiry exclusively under c.tokenMu (race-free under -race) and redact appSecret, operator unionId, and access tokens from error messages.

Resource references and upstream workspace/node/dentry/space/document IDs reject empty, untrimmed, control-character, and dot-segment ('.', '..') values before URL path interpolation with url.PathEscape.

Pre-signed OSS/CDN attachment downloads use an SSRF-safe client that never attaches DingTalk API tokens, validates pre-signed header names/values against control characters without echoing secret signatures in errors, and caps body reads via io.LimitReader.
Cursor pagination across workspaces, wiki nodes, and document blocks enforces seen-token cycle detection and hard page limits.

findings.summary: doJSON invalidated c.token and c.tokenExpiry on HTTP 401 without holding c.tokenMu and redact() read c.token unlocked while concurrent goroutines refreshed tokens, causing a Go data race under -race.

decodeResourceReference and DingTalk API path builders accepted dot-segment IDs ('.', '..') enabling URL path traversal, and fetchSigned passed unvalidated upstream pre-signed header values to net/http (which echoes raw header secrets in control-character errors).

invariants_checked: Feishu/Lark BaseURL configuration trims trailing slashes and whitespace, enforces ValidateConnectorBaseURL SSRF/userinfo/query/fragment checks, synchronizes tenant_access_token refresh under mutex, and redacts app_secret and access tokens.

All wiki, docx, drive, bitable, board, export, and contact API calls validate token/ID segments (rejecting '.', '..', '/', '\\', '?', '#', and control characters) and escape both URL path segments (url.PathEscape) and query parameters (url.QueryEscape).

Recursive wiki node walks track visited node tokens to break cyclic parent/child graphs, and paginated list loops across wiki spaces/nodes, drive files, docx blocks, and bitable records enforce repeated page_token detection, empty-page limits, and maxFeishuPaginationHops bounds.
All API JSON payloads and media/export downloads are bounded via io.LimitReader with GENYEE User-Agent headers and zero legacy brand residues.

findings.summary: Feishu core API methods interpolated spaceID, nodeToken, documentID, fileToken, ticket, appToken, tableID, whiteboardID, userID, and pagination page_token directly into URL paths and raw query strings without dot-segment/separator validation or url.PathEscape/url.QueryEscape, and Config.GetBaseURL did not strip trailing slashes.

listAllWikiNodesRecursive and listWikiNodeDescendants recursed indefinitely on cyclic wiki node graphs without a visited set, and listDocumentBlocks / readBitableRecords lacked repeated page_token and max pagination hop guards when upstream repeated HasMore=true.

invariants_checked: Drive folder traversal in ResolveResourceAncestors, buildDriveAncestorChain, and recursive file listing tracks visited folder tokens so cyclic parent/child metadata from upstream cannot trigger infinite API recursion.

Compound resource identifiers ('rootFolder:itemToken') fail closed when rootFolderToken is empty (e.g. ':subA') in both ListResources and listDriveFilesForResource instead of listing the tenant root folder.
Incremental sync cursor tracking, file size limits, and GENYEE metadata contracts pass cleanly under -race.

findings.summary: ResolveResourceAncestors and buildDriveAncestorChain lacked visited-folder cycle guards (recursing infinitely on cyclic Drive folder graphs), and ListResources / listDriveFilesForResource accepted malformed ':token' IDs with an empty rootFolderToken (falling open to tenant root listing).

invariants_checked: ResolveResourceAncestors tracks visited parent_node_token values and enforces a hard depth cap (256) so cyclic ParentNodeID chains from GetWikiNode terminate deterministically.
Compound wiki resource IDs ('spaceID:nodeToken') fail closed when spaceID is empty in ListResources and FetchAll/FetchIncremental.
Exported document and whiteboard assets obey Feishu core SSRF and io.LimitReader bounds and pass -race.

findings.summary: ResolveResourceAncestors walked ParentNodeID chains via GetWikiNode without a visited set or depth bound (looping infinitely on cyclic parent pointers), and ListResources / wikiOps.List accepted ':nodeToken' resource IDs with an empty spaceID.

invariants_checked: Self-hosted and SaaS GitLab BaseURLs pass ValidateConnectorBaseURL SSRF/userinfo/query/fragment checks, PRIVATE-TOKEN credentials reject control characters without leaking secrets in errors, and cross-origin redirects strip auth headers.

Project IDs (numeric or namespace/project paths), git refs, and repository paths reject dot-segment traversal ('.', '..', 'group/../admin', percent-encoded '%2e%2e'), query/fragment delimiters, backslashes, and control characters before url.PathEscape encoding.

Repository tree walks track visited directory paths and cap total walked directories (maxWalkDirs = 10000) to prevent cyclic submodule/tree loops, and both raw and base64-fallback file downloads enforce c.rawLimit on decoded payload bytes.

findings.summary: GitLab project_id, ref, and ListResources parentID accepted raw and percent-encoded dot-segments ('..', 'group/../admin', '../etc') and query/fragment characters, and newClient accepted control characters in PRIVATE-TOKEN headers (risking secret exposure via net/http header errors).

walkFiles recursed into repository tree entries without tracking visited directory paths or bounding directory count (looping infinitely on cyclic tree responses), and client.raw's base64 JSON fallback allocated base64FileBytes(c.rawLimit) (+1024 bytes slack) without re-checking len(decoded) > c.rawLimit after base64 decoding.

invariants_checked: IMA OpenAPI BaseURL enforces ValidateConnectorBaseURL SSRF validation, ClientID/APIKey and pre-signed COS download headers reject control characters without echoing secrets, and COS downloads run through a dedicated SSRF-safe HTTP client bounded by io.LimitReader.

Bare web-bookmark items (mediaTypeWeb with empty Content) validate upstream URLInfo.URL via validateIMARemoteURL (enforcing http/https, no embedded userinfo, no control characters, and ValidateURLForSSRF) before populating FetchedItem.URL for downstream CreateKnowledgeFromURL ingestion.

Knowledge-base folder recursion in listAllKBFiles tracks visited folder IDs and caps folder count (maxFoldersPerKB = 10000), cursor pagination detects repeated cursors, and FetchIncremental fails closed on nil DataSourceConfig.

findings.summary: Connector.FetchIncremental dereferenced config.ResourceIDs before checking config == nil (panicking on nil config), and listAllKBFiles recursed into sub-folders without tracking visited folder IDs or capping folder count on cyclic upstream folder graphs.

fetchOneMedia emitted bare web-link items (Content=nil, URL=detail.URLInfo.URL) without scheme/userinfo/SSRF validation — allowing upstream-supplied http://169.254.169.254/... or file:///... URLs to reach downstream CreateKnowledgeFromURL — and parseIMAConfig / DownloadURL lacked control-character validation on credentials and signed headers.

invariants_checked: WebDAV BaseURL and PROPFIND/GET requests enforce SSRF safe-dialer validation, restrict redirects to same-origin within the user's DAV root so Basic-Auth credentials never leak cross-origin or across DAV roots, and redact app passwords and usernames from errors/logs.

PROPFIND XML parsing uses bounded io.LimitReader bodies with strict XML decoder entity/token protections (no XXE or billion-laughs expansion) and validates href path containment against dot-segment escape.

Directory traversal enforces maxTraversalDepth (256), maxTraversalEntries (1,000,000), canonical path deduplication, per-file size caps, and streaming checkpoint cancellation propagation cleanly under -race.

Notion API BaseURL trims trailing slashes, enforces ValidateConnectorBaseURL SSRF/userinfo/query/fragment checks, rejects control characters in Integration/OAuth tokens without echoing secrets, and strips Authorization headers on cross-origin redirects.

All page, database, data-source, and block IDs are validated via validateNotionID (rejecting empty, dot-segment, slash, query/fragment, and control-character inputs) and escaped with url.PathEscape, and start_cursor query parameters are escaped with url.QueryEscape.

S3/external file downloads via DownloadFile reject embedded userinfo without leaking credentials, enforce SSRF validation and io.LimitReader caps, and computeExcludedSet breaks cyclic parent relationships deterministically without hanging.

findings.summary: Notion API methods interpolated pageID, databaseID, dataSourceID, and blockID into /v1/... paths without dot-segment/separator validation or url.PathEscape, concatenated unescaped start_cursor into query strings, did not trim trailing slashes in extractBaseURL/newClient, and accepted control characters in api_key.

computeExcludedSet walked parentMap chains without a visited-node guard (hanging indefinitely on cyclic parent pointers), and DownloadFile accepted URLs with embedded userinfo and echoed raw parse errors.

invariants_checked: RSS/Atom/JSON feed fetches and readability article fetches run through SSRF-safe HTTP clients with 10 MiB / 5 MiB io.LimitReader body caps, custom AuthHeaders are sent exclusively to configured feed URLs (never to article links), and parseConfig/fetch reject embedded userinfo, non-http(s) schemes, and header control characters without echoing secrets.

resolveItem sanitizes item.Link and strips non-http(s), userinfo-bearing, and SSRF-blocked links before populating FetchedItem.URL / Metadata['link'] so empty-summary feed items cannot smuggle internal/metadata URLs into downstream CreateKnowledgeFromURL.

FetchIncremental guards nil DataSourceConfig with ErrInvalidConfig, and walk propagates outer caller context cancellation immediately across both feed and per-item article loops rather than mistaking cancelled article fetches for transient fallback-to-summary failures.

findings.summary: FetchIncremental dereferenced config.ResourceIDs before checking config == nil (panicking on nil config), and walk swallowed caller context cancellation inside resolveItem's fallback-to-summary path instead of aborting the sync loop immediately.

resolveItem copied raw item.Link into FetchedItem.URL even when extractArticle rejected the URL or feedContent was empty (allowing http://169.254.169.254/..., javascript:..., or userinfo URLs to reach CreateKnowledgeFromURL), and parseConfig/fetch lacked userinfo and control-character validation with secret-redacted errors.

invariants_checked: Seafile API BaseURL and seafhttp file-server download links enforce SSRF safe-dialer validation, reject userinfo/query/fragment/control characters, never forward API Authorization tokens to seafhttp signed download URLs, and redact tokens and signed links from sync logs and error items.

Repo UUIDs and directory/file paths enforce strict format and canonical path validation (rejecting dot-segments, backslashes, duplicate names, and negative sizes), and file downloads enforce io.LimitReader caps against utils.GetMaxFileSize().

walkDir enforces both maxTraversalDepth (256) and maxTraversalEntries (1,000,000) so runaway or cyclic Seafile directory listings abort cleanly with ErrFetchFailed without emitting spurious reconcile deletions.

findings.summary: Unlike nextcloud/sync.go, Seafile's walkDir pushed subdirectory paths onto its traversal stack without bounding directory nesting depth (maxTraversalDepth) or total enumerated entries (maxTraversalEntries), allowing a misbehaving or cyclic self-hosted Seafile server to recurse until context timeout or OOM.

invariants_checked: Yuque public and enterprise BaseURLs enforce ValidateConnectorBaseURL SSRF/userinfo/query/fragment checks, X-Auth-Token values reject control characters without echoing tokens in errors and log only redacted prefixes once per client, and all JSON responses are capped at 16 MiB via readCapped.

User and group logins in ListUserRepos / ListGroupRepos reject empty, untrimmed, dot-segment ('.', '..'), slash/backslash, query/fragment, and control-character inputs and apply url.PathEscape; numeric userID, bookID, and docID parameters use integer formatting.

Offset pagination in listReposPaginated and ListBookDocs enforces maxPaginationHops (10000) and repeated-first-ID stall detection, buildTOCPaths enforces visited-UUID cycle protection and maxTOCDepth (32), truncate backs off to UTF-8 rune boundaries, and FetchIncremental guards nil DataSourceConfig.

findings.summary: Connector.FetchIncremental dereferenced config.ResourceIDs before checking config == nil (panicking on nil config), ListUserRepos and ListGroupRepos interpolated raw login strings into /api/v2/{users,groups}/%s/repos without dot-segment/separator validation or url.PathEscape, and parseYuqueConfig accepted control characters in api_token.
